title: Service account lifecycle and least-privilege templates for RBAC v2
text:
Service account lifecycle and least-privilege templates for RBAC v2

description:
Goal: Add first-class service account (SA) admin controls as part of RBAC v2 so customers can create, own, audit, and operate SAs with least-privilege templates. Scope: API/Console/CLI creation flows, ownership assignment & transfer, baked-in least-privilege templates, automatic audit events for lifecycle actions, key/token rotation UI/endpoint, and guardrails for unsafe grants. Out of scope: Federated identity provider onboarding (separate initiative).

acceptance_criteria:
1) Customers can create SAs via Console/API/CLI and select a named least-privilege template. 2) SA creation, key issuance, permission changes, ownership transfers, rotations, and deletion are emitted to audit logs with actor, timestamp, and request metadata. 3) Ownership transfer must require owner acknowledgement and admin approval if the SA has high-scope permissions. 4) Console shows template rationale and permissions in human-readable form. 5) Default templates prevent broad org-level write unless explicitly escalated via an approval workflow. 6) Backwards compatibility: existing service-account tokens remain valid until rotation/deletion and are visible in the migration guide.

design_decisions:
- Templates are predefined sets of RBAC grants (resource-scoped) and cannot be edited by non-admins; editing requires a separate template-management ticket. - Use resource-scoped role granularity: model:<model-id>:/invoke, project:<project-id>:/read, org:/billing:read. - Audit logs recorded to existing audit sink with a new event namespace 'service_account.lifecycle'. - Owner semantics: each SA has exactly one owner user or team; removal triggers a 7-day orphaned-grace period. - Key management: short-lived tokens by default (90 days) with auto-rotation hooks to KMS. - UI flows expose least-privilege warnings and require explicit confirmation for high-scope templates.

tradeoffs:
- Tight templates improve security but increase friction for quick prototyping; mitigated by allowing temporary 'escalation grants' that expire. - Short-lived tokens require rotation automation; we will provide rotation endpoints/CLI helpers to ease adoption. - Storing template definitions centrally reduces duplication but requires migration for custom templates from v1.

implementation_notes:
API endpoints: POST /orgs/:org/service-accounts, GET /orgs/:org/service-accounts/:id, PATCH /orgs/:org/service-accounts/:id (owner, description), POST /orgs/:org/service-accounts/:id/keys (issue token), POST /orgs/:org/service-accounts/:id/keys/:key_id/rotate, POST /orgs/:org/service-accounts/:id/transfer. Console: creation wizard with template selector, owner selector, optional rationale field. CLI: rhubarb sa create --template=infer-only --owner=team-platform --ttl=90d. Audit schema: event_type, sa_id, action (create, issue_key, rotate, transfer, delete), actor_id, actor_type, timestamp, request_id, ip, old_owner, new_owner, template_name.

least_privilege_templates:
Planned templates (names + short descriptions): 1) infer-only: invoke models scoped to selected projects (no read of logs or billing). 2) embeddings-readonly: generate embeddings only, per-model scope. 3) monitoring-exporter: read-only metrics & trace export to granted sinks. 4) billing-reporter: read billing usage, export CSVs. 5) admin-cli-temporary: broad access for 1 week with mandatory approval. These will map to RBAC v2 role IDs in the release notes.

migration_plan:
1) Inventory current SAs (v1) and map their permissions to closest templates; generate a migration report. 2) Notify owners and create recommended template-based replacements. 3) Provide opt-in automated migration script for low-risk SAs. 4) Mark unmigrated high-scope SAs and require manual review before RBAC v2 enforcement.

security_controls:
- Enforce KMS-backed secrets for long-lived keys. - Mandatory audit event emission on all lifecycle changes. - Admin-only endpoints for template creation and template edits. - Escalation approval workflow for templates that grant org-level write permissions (requires 2 approvers). - Periodic owner-validation job that pings owners; orphaned SAs are disabled after a grace window.

observability:
- New dashboard in Console: Service accounts overview with last-used, owner, template, scope, and days-since-last-key-rotation. - Alerts: SA with unused token >180 days, SA with owner change, failed rotation attempts. - Audit sink: separate index for service_account.lifecycle to support fast forensic queries.

rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (alpha, internal): UI + API + audit events for create/issue/rotate + basic templates. Phase 2 (beta, selected customers): ownership transfer flows, orphaning job, console dashboard. Phase 3 (general): approval workflows, template management UI, migration tooling. Feature flag gating per org and feature-rollout by percentage.

risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: accidental privilege escalation during migration. Mitigation: read-only migration recommendations, migration dry-run, owner confirmation windows. Risk: audit log spam from bulk token rotations. Mitigation: aggregate rotation events in dashboard and sample raw events for forensic queries.

updates:
2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting with Security and Product. Agreed on resource-scoped grants and owner semantics (Aisha, Marco, Priya).
2026-02-25: API contract draft reviewed. Added /transfer endpoint and orphaning grace window requirement. Action: Marco to prototype API handlers (ENG-4851).
2026-03-02: Design review with Console team. Console wizard mockups approved with minor wording changes (DES-2143).
2026-03-05: Security review pre-check: require KMS for long-lived tokens and 2-approver escalation for org write templates. Security review scheduled.
2026-03-10: Initial backend PR opened: create SA + issue key + audit event plumbing (github.com/redwood-inference/rbi/pull/6792). Running unit tests; integration tests pending.
Blockers: need final decision on default token TTL (90d vs 30d). Security prefers 30d; product prefers 90d for developer ergonomics. Decision pending by security council on 2026-03-17.

comments:
Priya Malhotra: Please ensure template names are stable IDs; we'll need them surfaced in billing and cadence reports.
Jordan Lee: For the orphaning flow, prefer sending an email + Slack pings before auto-disable. Include audit events for each contact attempt.
Marco Chen: PR #6792 implements token issuance and audit events. Need help wiring rotation to KMS from infra team (INC-1225).
Aisha Patel: Add migration dry-run CSV export for org admins so they can review mappings before committing.
Security Team (note): Approval required for templates granting org:*/write. Mark 'admin-cli-temporary' as requiring 2 approvers and auto-expiry.
